note: An UNDECLARED item is not read yet and is not a fault. A DECLARED item nothing reaches is a hole, and that is what this file is for. The Calumet Club reception rosters declare themselves in receptions.json, which carries a `roster_read` flag per reception and names which rosters are read (1879 and 1882) and which are not (1880, 1881); this file starts with T-0574 because a list read out of a page needs a line range and a count, which a reception row has nowhere to put.

declarations.what: The OBITUARY printed in Robert Fergus's Directory of the City of Chicago, Illinois, for 1843 (Fergus Printing Company, 1896) — "Names, places, dates, and ages at death of some of Chicago's Old Settlers" — in K. Torp's 2007 transcription on Genealogy Trails: one web page, cached at data/research/old_settlers/text/fergus_1843_old_settler_death_notices.txt. Lines 14-813, which are the twenty-three letter sections and every entry under them. Every entry is a record.
declarations.entries_checked_by: tools/read_fergus_obits.py --check, which re-segments the committed text and fails when it yields a different number than this file declares. A declared list that quietly loses forty entries is the hole coverage exists to catch, and a count is the only thing that catches it.
declarations.counts_differ_from_the_ticket_and_why: T-0574 was sized off inventory.json's line-shaped estimate of 743 entries. Read entry by entry the page yields 757, and the difference is segmentation, not discovery: the estimate counted lines, and this reading counts entries. It joins the 20 lines that are the turn of a long entry — the transcription wraps but does not indent, so "Aug. 1, 1860, aged 55-7-11." under K and "Oct. 12, 1877, a. 55-1-11." under O are turns and not men — and it opens entries at the eleven heads the printer or the transcriber set without a comma after the surname ("Kimberly Col. John Ellis", "Kirk James Smith", "Scott. Maj. Martin", "Sweet Richard M.", "Saint Cyr", "Little Turtle" and five more) and at the one whose surname carries a particle ("Van de Velde, Rt.-Rev. Jas. Oliver", which a rule stopping at the first word folded into the entry above him). The inventory estimate is left as it stands; this declaration is what was actually read.

not_read_and_why.lines 1-13: The transcriber's banner, the list's title and header, the bracketed source note naming the 1843 directory and the 1896 Fergus Printing Company reprint, the transcriber's credit, and the A-Z navigation. The header is not filed as a record because it is a statement about the LIST rather than about a person — it is quoted verbatim on the records file, on the crosswalk and on every record, because it is the limit the whole reading turns on. The bracketed source note is on the source record.
not_read_and_why.lines 814-816: "Robert Fergus, Compiler", "©2007 Kim Torp" and "Illinois Genealogy Trails" — the compiler's name and the transcriber's footer.
not_read_and_why.the rest of the 1843 volume: The business and alphabetical directories are READ, under T-0571, into data/research/directories/. The civic and statistical account of printed page 1 is declared unread there and owned by T-0589.

declarations.what: The printed REGISTER of the Calumet Club's first Old Settlers' reception — "NAMES OF OLD SETTLERS OF CHICAGO, REGISTERED AT THE CALUMET CLUB", Early Chicago (Chicago, 1879), printed pages 83-90 — read entry by entry off the page images of the Internet Archive copy earlychicagorece00calu, and the three aggregate tables of printed page 72 (PLACES OF BIRTH, YEARS OF ARRIVAL, AGES) read off the same plate. Transcribed at data/research/old_settlers/text/calumet_club_1879_registry.txt: printed pages 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89 and 90 entire, one line per registrant in the plate's five columns, plus 60 aggregate cells. Every entry is a record.
declarations.entries_checked_by: tools/old_settlers.py --check, which re-reads the committed transcription and fails when people.json no longer matches it, and --self-test, which proves that assertion still fires against a damaged cell and a deleted deposit.
declarations.counts_differ_from_the_ticket_and_why: T-0577 was written from the proceedings' own sentence, "one hundred and forty-nine registered their names", and expected 149 names. The printed register carries 159. The document explains its own difference on the same page — "Many left without knowing that there was a registry being kept. A few called afterward and signed the registry" — and all three aggregate tables sum to exactly 149, so the tables count the evening and the register is the fuller book. Which ten entries are the later signers is NOT stated by the plate and is not guessed: receptions.json's reconciliation_1879 carries the printed and the read count of every table cell side by side, and the differences are not all positive, so the tables are not a clean subset of the register either.

not_read_and_why.printed page 83: the register's own half-title, "NAMES OF THE SETTLERS OF CHICAGO, WHO CAME PRIOR TO 1840, REGISTERED AT THE CALUMET CLUB OF CHICAGO" — a statement about the list, quoted in the transcription's header and filed as no record.
not_read_and_why.printed pages 1-71 and 73-82: the proceedings themselves — the officers and members of the club, the invitation, the prayer, and the speeches of Beggs, Strong, Caton, Blodgett, Grant, Wentworth, Goodrich, Scammon and Bross, with the appendix of letters from Watkins, Towner, Bascom, Hunter, Peck and Porter and the Tribune and Evening Journal reports. NOT read. These are old settlers' recollections of the town this project builds, and Wentworth's alone runs to seventeen pages: they are a reading pass of their own, and the OCR text layer is sound in the prose, so that pass does not need the page images.
